a11y.apg: No APG pattern: it is <pre><code>, and native semantics are what a screen reader needs — the <pre> preserves the line structure that the code depends on. Without `copyable` there is nothing to focus. With it, the copy button is a real <button> with an accessible name, reachable by Tab like any other.

props.name: children
props.description: The code, as a string and not as nodes: it goes verbatim inside <code>, so whitespace and line breaks are yours to control.

props.name: language
props.description: Written to data-language, which is what labels the block. It does not highlight — the component is a display, not a parser.

props.name: copyable
props.description: Draws the copy button. The copying itself lives in the core's aurea.js, so React and plain HTML share one implementation instead of two that drift.

props.name: className
props.description: Lands on the outer element either way — on the <pre> when plain, on the wrapper when copyable.
